independent.summary: The new comment claims "Cases A, B and C still exercise the absorption path", but C is false: C's fixture (SEC_A+H2_A ≈ 1190 + SEC_B section 206 ≈ 1400 chars) now fits under CHUNK_MAX, so mergeTargetFor returns Infinity and C produces a single chunk via the normal push — exactly what the rewritten D asserts for the same text. C therefore no longer reaches flushMergeBuf(true)'s absorption branch (it passes for a new reason, so its title no longer describes what it tests), and with E/F also reshaped, nothing in the suite now covers appendToLast carrying an absorbed section's anchor into extraAnchors — the LEO-102 regression guard the file exists for. A/B only cover the splitOversizedSection absorption, which passes no anchors.

The synthesised "[H1] Subject" paragraph is prepended to page text before thin-page detection, and that detection measures filtered paragraph length (embedPageData: filtered.join('\n\n').length < THIN_PAGE_THRESHOLD, 300) with headings exempt from keepPara's length floor. An H1-less thin page with ~260–299 chars of real content plus a 20–40 char title now measures over 300, so it is chunked and embedded individually instead of being grouped under its parent URL — the exact regression the multi-URL thin-page grouping was built to prevent. estimateContentLen (used at scraper.js:1092 and :1162) has the same inflation.

TITLE_SEP_RE treats breadcrumb separators '>' and '»' as page/site separators and then takes the leftmost non-brand part, so a breadcrumb <title> like "Home > Camps > Men's Retreat" yields pageH1 "Home" — the subject is on the right of a breadcrumb, the same reasoning the module applies to deliberately exclude ':'. The result is a wrong subject line injected into the header of every chunk on every H1-less page of such a site, which is worse for retrieval than the no-H1 state the rule is meant to fix.

questions.json is the committed set of "universal small-business questions" that rag-eval runs against every domain, scoring a per-domain hit-rate with no notion of an expected miss. Adding an entity-specific church question permanently books one guaranteed miss against dosiedough.com, burkdigital.com, tomatopiecafe.com etc., lowering the shared baseline every future RAG change is measured against and making new scorecards non-comparable with prior runs. The harness already accepts --questions <path> for an ad-hoc set.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication, authorization or session code is touched — the diff is scraper chunking, a new pure helper module, tests and fixtures.
The only .env.example addition is CHUNK_SHAPE_LOG_LEVEL, a log verbosity knob, not a credential, and no secret handling changes.
No billing, Stripe, quota or pricing code is in the diff.
No deletes, migrations or data-destroying operations are added or modified; the chunk insert-before-delete path is untouched.
No external API call sites change — the Puppeteer evaluate block only additionally returns document.title, and embeddings/Claude call sites are untouched.
No version bump, deploy config, package.json or build file changes; the new env var ships with a safe in-code default.

summary: The local review found nothing and its triage is entirely correct but trivially so; it missed the real issue — that rewriting cases C/E/F silently deleted the suite's only coverage of the absorbed-anchor path while a new comment asserts the opposite — plus three smaller defects.
